div.head: Hn Lond 6
div.ab: Et ecclesię et barones et ciues habeant et teneant bene et in pace socnas suas cum omnibus consuetudinibus, ita quod hospites, qui in soccis hospitantur, nulli dent consuetudines nisi illi cuius socca fuerit uel ministro suo quem ibi posuerit.

Et ecclesiae et barones et cives teneant et habeant bene et in pace socnas suas cum omnibus consuetudinibus, ita quod hospites, qui in soccis hospitabuntur, nulli dent consuetudines nisi illi cuius soca fuerit vel ministro suo quem ibi posuerit.

And the churches and barons and citizens shall have and hold in peace and security their rights of jurisdiction along with all their dues, in such a way that lessees who occupy property in districts under private jurisdiction shall pay dues to no-one except the man to whom the jurisdiction belongs, or to the official whom he has placed there.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 290–291 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 525, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Das Kapitel zielt nicht etwa auf Unterdrückung fremder Händler (wie Norton Comment. 273 meint), sondern auf Erhaltung der unabhängigen Enklaven innerhalb Londons (s. d. Gl 28a) zugunsten feudaler Gewalten; deutlicher s. Lib. civ. 4.—Dies Kapitel fehlt Londons späteren Freibriefen.—Kirchen mit eigenem, aus der Stadt eximiertem Boden samt privater Gerichtsbarkeit waren u. a. der Dom, St. Martin le Grand, die Knighten Gild, der später die Dreifaltigkeitspriorei zu Aldgate im Rechte nachfolgte, Westminster (s. u. zu 8{c}), Chertsey, das Manor Lambeth; vgl. Ballard Br. bor. char. 125—29; Engl. bor. 12. cty. 54

The chapter aims not, say, at suppressing foreign traders (as Norton Comment. 273 thinks), but at preserving the independent enclaves within London (see that word in Gl 28a) in favour of feudal powers; more clearly, see Lib. civ. 4.—This chapter is absent from London's later charters.—Churches with their own land exempted from the city, together with private jurisdiction, included the cathedral, St. Martin le Grand, the Knighten Gild (whose rights later passed to the Priory of Holy Trinity at Aldgate), Westminster (see below on 8{c}), Chertsey, and the manor of Lambeth; cf. Ballard Br. bor. char. 125—29; Engl. bor. 12. cty. 54

Nicht etwa im engen späteren Sinne ‘Patrizier [Londons]’, etwa Aldermen (Norton 262. 291. 340), sondern Kronvassallen wie die Erzbischöfe, der Bischof, die Äbte (s. o.{a}) und Adlige wie Fitz Walter, der Kommandant von Castle Baynard, Montfichet; Munim. Gildhal. I 64. 610. II 150. Dahinter heisst cives nicht (wie o. 1. 2. 3) ‘alle Bürger, die gesamte Bürgerschaft’, sondern hier ‘jeder von jenen einzelnen Bürgern, welche jurisdiktionell privilegierten Boden besitzen (namentlich vielleicht die Aldermen)’, laut der 3 Sing. am Satzende illi cuius .. uel posuerit. Ich halte die Bezirke im Besitz dieser ecclesiae, barones und cives, nicht (mit Stubbs Lect. 126) ganz London bedeckend, sondern nur für Enklaven innerhalb der Mauer, die ausserhalb der politischen Macht der Stadtgemeinde damals noch verbleiben

Not, say, in the narrow later sense ‘patricians [of London]’, for instance aldermen (Norton 262. 291. 340), but tenants-in-chief such as the archbishops, the bishop, the abbots (see above{a}), and nobles such as Fitz Walter, the commander of Castle Baynard, and Montfichet; Munim. Gildhal. I 64. 610. II 150. After them cives does not mean (as above 1. 2. 3) ‘all citizens, the whole citizen body’, but here ‘each of those individual citizens who own land privileged as to jurisdiction (perhaps notably the aldermen)’, as the 3rd sing. at the end of the sentence shows: illi cuius .. uel posuerit. I take the districts in the possession of these ecclesiae, barones and cives not (with Stubbs Lect. 126) as covering the whole of London, but only as enclaves within the wall which at that time still remained outside the political power of the city community

Hintersassen, Mieter innerhalb der Enklaven, unter Zoll und Gerichtsbarkeit (s. d. Gl 26e) des Grundherrn der socn (Jurisdiktionsbezirk), nicht etwa nur Ausländer oder nur nicht in London Gebürtige, sondern ‘Nicht-Untertanen der Stadtbehörde, obwohl in London wohnhaft, weil Untertanen des Herrschaftsbodens einer Kirche, eines Barons, eines Privileg-Bürgers’

Under-tenants, lodgers within the enclaves, subject to the toll and jurisdiction (see that word in Gl 26e) of the lord of the socn (district of jurisdiction); not, say, only foreigners or only those not born in London, but ‘persons not subject to the city authority, though resident in London, because subject to the lordship land of a church, a baron or a privileged citizen’
Vgl. Gl London 28a; Stadt 8; Adelsbeamter 10
Cf. Gl London 28a; Stadt 8; Adelsbeamter 10
